stops.name: Munich, On the Deities of Samothrace, the descent into myth
stops.campa: Before the Bavarian Academy Schelling reads On the Deities of Samothrace, plunging into the dark Cabiri, the primal hungering gods of the Samothracian mysteries, seeking in the oldest cults the ladder by which the divine ascends into being. It is a fragment torn from the vast unfinished Ages of the World, over whose first book he labours and despairs, printing and suppressing draft after draft. The philosopher of nature has become the archaeologist of God's own past, digging beneath the light for the ground of all things.

stops.name: Erlangen, the lectures in the wilderness
stops.campa: From 1820 Schelling lectures at Erlangen, holding still his Munich post. In these small Franconian halls he turns from the finished systems of his youth toward a new thing: the Philosophy of Mythology, the idea that the gods of the nations are not errors but a true theogonic process working itself out in human consciousness. The seed of the final philosophy of revelation is sown in near-obscurity, spoken to few, while the age looks the other way.

stops.name: Munich, the new university chair, positive philosophy
stops.campa: The Bavarian university is moved to Munich and Schelling takes a chair there, drawing crowds again as the old lion of German thought. He forges the distinction that will crown his life: negative philosophy, which thinks only what a thing must be, against positive philosophy, which thinks the fact that it is: the free act of a living God who reveals himself in history. The dead Hegel's system, he prophesies, cannot cross from thought to existence. Schelling prepares his return.

stops.name: Berlin, summoned to slay the dragon of Hegelianism
stops.campa: The King of Prussia calls the aged Schelling to Berlin, to the very chair where Hegel taught and died, expressly to root out the pantheism and the revolution that have grown from Hegel's school. On the fifteenth of November he mounts the rostrum before an overflowing hall. In the audience sit Kierkegaard, Engels, Bakunin, Burckhardt, Humboldt: the whole coming century, listening. The old man who once planted a Tree of Liberty is set against the shade of his oldest friend, to speak the Philosophy of Revelation.
stops.quote: I am so glad to have heard Schelling's second lecture — indescribable. When he mentioned the word 'actuality' the child of thought leaped for joy within me as in Elizabeth.
stops.quote_source: Søren Kierkegaard, journal / letter, Berlin, November 1841

stops.name: Berlin, the Philosophy of Revelation, and disillusion
stops.campa: Through the winter Schelling unfolds the Philosophy of Mythology and of Revelation: the descent of the divine into history, Christ as the turning of the ages, myth fulfilled in the incarnate God. But the young Hegelians turn on him. Engels writes his savage pamphlet Schelling and Revelation; Kierkegaard sickens of the 'insufferable nonsense' and departs. When Paulus pirates the lectures verbatim, Schelling, robbed of his words, falls silent and lectures no more. The last great effort ends in wounded quiet.

stops.name: Bad Ragaz, death at the healing waters
stops.campa: In the summer of his eightieth year Schelling comes to the Swiss spa of Bad Ragaz, to the healing springs of the Tamina gorge under the Alps. There, on the twentieth of August, the last of the great German idealists lays down his life: the boy of Leonberg, the youth of the attic room, the professor at twenty-three, the philosopher of nature and freedom and revelation. King Maximilian of Bavaria raises over his grave a stone that names him the first thinker of Germany. Nature, made visible spirit, receives him.
